items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: On bass was a gentleman by the name of Gene Ramey I think, either Gene Ramey or Al Hall. My memory is hazy there. And of course Freddie Green, Count Basie, and Gus Johnson was the drummer.

ctx.x: On bass was a gentleman by the name of Gene Ramey I think, either Gene Ramey or Al Hall. My memory is hazy there. And of course Freddie Green, Count Basie, and Gus Johnson was the drummer. Now proceed.

items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: The interviewee does not speak about Freddie Green; the mention is made entirely by the interviewer.

ctx.x: His simplistic piano style, and very understated, and a very happy feeling. When he first went to Kansas City and he heard this happy music and he fell in love with it and he wanted to be a part of it, well he, that feeling just osmosed into him and he osmosed it back.
And when they finally added on Freddie Green, Basie was able to give up a lot of stuff with his left hand, and just tinkled, you know and Freddie was going on with the straight 4/4.
